US forces disable ship ‘attempting to run’ Iran blockade in Gulf of Oman
US military jet strikes stern of commercial cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman ‘without harming the crew’, CENTCOM says.
United States forces have disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman after its crew “ignored repeated warnings and attempted to run the ongoing naval blockade against Iran”, according to Central Command (CENTCOM).
A US military fighter jet struck the stern of the Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica, also known as the Arika Sun, with a precision munition on Saturday, “fully disabling the ship’s propulsion without harming the crew”, CENTCOM said in a statement. The vessel was attempting to transit regional waters after “having previously departed an Iranian port”.
CENTCOM said its forces resumed their blockade against all ships “entering or departing Iranian ports on July 14”, disabling four commercial vessels and turning around 135 ships during “three months of strict enforcement”.
US forces also destroyed 10 tankers linked to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ (IRGC) “multibillion-dollar shadow network” over the same period, CENTCOM said.
US Senator Chris Murphy questioned the military strike, writing on X: “What is this all for? Why are taxpayers paying billions to hit commercial ships?”
“Apparently the goal is to gain leverage in order to convince the Iranians to let us pay them billions to return everything to the way it all was before the war,” the Democratic politician added. “What a disaster.”
The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency acknowledged the incident on Sunday, saying that it had received “a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman” and that authorities were investigating.
Meanwhile, the IRGC said it struck a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz for attempting to take an “illegal route”, as Tehran seeks to enforce its own blockade on the vital waterway.
In a statement carried by official Iranian media, the IRGC claimed Iranian forces “have taken control of the administration of the strait”.
“In carrying out this mission, a few hours ago, a giant LPG carrier named NV Sunshine, owned by NatWit, which was attempting to transit via the illegal route south of the Strait of Hormuz, was struck,” the statement said.
The UKMTO said on Sunday that an outbound tanker in the strait was struck on the port side by an unknown projectile, causing a fire on board. The UK agency said crew members were reported safe, while the damage and environmental impact remained unknown at the time of the report.
Tehran has attempted to enforce control over the Strait of Hormuz during the US-Israel war on Iran, insisting that ships obtain permission to cross via its preferred routes. However, vessels have increasingly risked taking an alternative route hugging the strait’s southern coast.
The UK maritime agency said on Thursday that a vessel sailing 94km (58 miles) north of Madinat ash Shamal, off the north coast of Qatar, was struck by multiple projectiles, resulting in several casualties.
The agency did not specify the origin of the ship or the number of people killed or injured, adding that authorities were investigating the incident amid a recent rise in attacks on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz.
Ships in the Gulf attempting to cross the strait, which is the sole maritime route in or out of the oil-rich region, have faced repeated attacks since the US and Israel began the war in late February.
The Strait of Hormuz remains vital to the global economy, with about a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas passing through the passage before the war began.

Qatar

Oman

Palestine

“I think we should have a baby.”
Noah whispered softly into the back of Sierra’s neck as they laid in bed on a lazy weekend morning. Sierra took his hand off her hips and pulled it tightly around her waist, snuggling back into him.
“Sounds like a plan, sweetie. We’ll get right on that.”
Noah waited a moment.
“I’m serious,” he finally said. “I think we should have a baby.”
Sierra’s body tensed under his embrace. She slowly unwrapped his arm from around her and turned to face him. “Honey,” she began. “I say this with all of the love and affection I can muster at 7am on a Saturday, but…what the fuck are you talking about?”
Noah rolled his eyes. “Oh, come on, don’t act like you’ve never thought about it. It seems like every time we listen to the news, there’s another story about another couple getting uncapped.”
“Well, yes,” Sierra responded, “but that’s because those people are out of their goddamn minds.” She sat up and rubbed her eyes. “This is a fantasy, right? We’re not actually having this conversation, are we?”
“Why not?” Noah replied a bit more sharply than he had intended. Then he caught himself. This wasn’t going how he had planned. He took a breath, pulled himself towards his wife, and took both of her hands in his. “I want a family. With you. I want us to make a baby, and watch it grow up, and teach it piano. This isn’t so crazy, is it?”
“Wanting those things? No, not crazy. But being foolish enough to actually pursue them? Yeah, a bit crazy.” She stood up and started to get dressed.
Noah sank back into bed and covered his face with his hands. “Come on, babe, don’t huff off like that. We’re married. We love each other. We can talk about important things without it turning into a fight, can’t we? I just wanted to start the conversation. Please, don’t be mad.”
Sierra found her house slippers and tied her silk robe. “Really? Don’t be mad? You just woke me up by announcing that you want to die. That you want me to die. And I’m supposed to find that…romantic, or something? Well pardon me for not swooning.”
Noah’s resolve eroded in the face of her withering look. “Jesus Christ,” he replied. “Don’t be so fucking dramatic. Of course I don’t want us to die. But guess what — sooner or later, we will! You could get hit by a bus tomorrow.”
Sierra laughed derisively. “Okay, sure. We’re both going to die,” she replied. “But you seem a bit more welcoming of the prospect than I am.”

Weeks went by. Sierra’s anger faded away and was slowly, eventually, replaced by something that surprised her — something more contemplative. She started to wonder whether it really was so crazy to trade in the sort of life she had for the chance to have a family. And as the days passed, she thought more and more about what it would feel like to be pregnant — to grow life inside of her — and she found herself wondering whether their child would have her eyes, or Noah’s chin.
It was the timing, really. If the discussion with Noah had happened …

Since its establishment, it has become one of the most prominent organizations involved in efforts to locate IDF soldiers abroad and file criminal complaints against them in various countries. However, only a handful of cases have resulted in preliminary procedural steps, with no convictions or significant indictments.

A sudden and unexpected change in our circumstances can leave us feeling distressed. We thought we…

A sudden and unexpected change in our circumstances can leave us feeling distressed. We thought we knew what our lives would be and we made plans on that basis, but now everything is uncertain. We became comfortable in our routines and habits, only to find that we are now overwhelmed by anxiety and stress.
Without our knowledge, we formed a deep attachment to beliefs about the status quo. We took its regularity for granted, and it now feels like a promise has been broken. We were promised consistency but we received chaos instead. Deep down, we might have known nothing was ever certain, but we never expected to face a change of this magnitude.
Attachment is so nefarious precisely because it easily goes unnoticed. We quietly become accustomed to a certain way of life and we fail to realize we are also becoming more rigid and resistant to movement. But the world will move and it will sometimes do so without warning. To be forced to move again after a long period of dormancy is necessarily shocking and suffering immediately follows — in this case, as anxiety and stress.

Man dies after entering tiger enclosure at England wildlife park
Emergency services called to the scene after reports of a man entering the tiger enclosure at a UK wildlife park.
A man has died after entering a tiger enclosure at a wildlife park in northern England and being attacked by one of the animals, police said.
South Yorkshire Police said officers and emergency medical staff were called to Yorkshire Wildlife Park near the city of Doncaster at about 1:35pm on Saturday (12:35 GMT) after receiving reports that a man had entered the enclosure.
He died at the scene. It was not immediately clear how he got in.
The tiger was not injured and stayed inside the enclosure during the incident, police said, adding that there was no wider risk to the public.
The park was evacuated, and officers remained at the scene on Saturday night.
“The man’s family is aware and is being supported by specialist officers. Our thoughts are with them at this distressing time,” police said in a statement.
Police also confirmed they were aware of footage circulating on social media that appeared to show the man inside the enclosure shortly before the attack, urging members of the public not to share the distressing video.
Tiger ‘will not be euthanised’
The park said it had closed after a serious incident involving the tiger enclosure and would remain closed until Sunday.
“We are working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened,” the park said in a statement on its website.
In another statement later on Sunday, the wildlife park offered its “thoughts and heartfelt sympathies” to the family of the man who was killed.
“The park will be closed today and the staff team who were deeply affected by events will receive specialist support,” it read. The park also confirmed that the tiger, named Altai, was “safe and well and will not be euthanised”.
Yorkshire Wildlife Park began operating in 2009, and its Land of the Tigers attraction – a purpose-built 0.4-hectare (2-acre) reserve for endangered Amur tigers, also known as Siberian tigers – opened in 2011.
A raised walkway, 300 metres (985 feet) long, lets visitors watch the tigers roam through woodland and grassland and play in a waterfall pool, the park said.

Hurricane Isaias leaves trail of destruction across the US Gulf Coast
Crews rally for massive cleanup efforts in Florida and Alabama as weakened Isaias leaves hundreds of thousands in the dark.
Residents across the southeastern United States have begun cleanup efforts after Hurricane Isaias, the first Atlantic tropical cyclone of the 2026 season, slammed ashore near Destin, Florida, on Friday.
As of midafternoon Sunday, roughly 356,000 customers remain without power in southern Alabama and the northwestern region of Florida, according to data from PowerOutage.com, an independent tracking website.
At its peak, the storm knocked out power to nearly 800,000 homes and businesses across the Gulf Coast.
Sarah Gatewood, a spokesperson for the utility company Florida Power and Light (FPL), announced that workers from across Florida and more than two dozen other states had mobilised to restore power.
At least four deaths have been linked to Isais after it made landfall as a Category 2 storm on the five-tier Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale.
The tempest churned northward into Alabama on Saturday with fierce tropical-storm-force winds before weakening into a post-tropical cyclone and tracking further north towards the Appalachians.
Though its power is waning, the storm continues to endanger the mid-Atlantic region with the potential for flash flooding.
According to the National Weather Service (NWS), surface observations indicate that Isaias now has maximum sustained winds of 160 km/h (100 mph) and an estimated minimum central pressure of 28.88 inches, or 978 millibars.
Across Florida and Alabama, residents have reported damage from the storm’s high-velocity winds.
A Rest and Relax Inn in the resort city of Pensacola, Florida, saw its roof sheared off during the hurricane, and a boathouse was flattened in Destin.
The immediate struggle for basic necessities was most stark in Pensacola, the westernmost part of the Florida Panhandle, where the storm downed power grids and caused widespread structural damage.
Hundreds of cars lined the block around a United Cajun Navy distribution site, a volunteer disaster relief organisation, on Saturday morning.
Pensacola’s Mayor DC Reeves warned of critical drinking water shortages following the storm, which affected drinking wells and water infrastructure. Residents, he said, remain under an advisory to boil tap water before use.
“We are winding down day three of storm response and recovery operations, and we remain focused on public safety, clearing debris, and restoring critical infrastructure and services,” Reeves said on social media.
Isaias also forced the indefinite closure of Pensacola International airport, Florida’s 10th-largest airfield, due to severe damage.
Fallen trees and power lines continue to make travel hazardous in Houston County, Alabama, which remains under an emergency flash flood warning, according to state emergency officials.
“Due to the impacts of Hurricane Isaias, all Houston County roads are closed until further notice,” the agency posted on X.
